title: [android][expo-image-picker] content:// URIs are not usable in `ExponentImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync`
body: ### Minimal reproducible example I don't have Android. I have no idea what is an `uri` with `content://` ### Summary "expo-image-picker": "~14.3.2", Exactly as it's happening here https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/9354, I'm getting an error in `ExponentImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync` ``` Call to function 'ExponentImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync' has been rejected. → Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://media/picker/0/com.android.providers.media.photopicker/media/1000043213 ``` For some reason, after upgrading to Expo 49, seems like the image picker totally changed (the UI) in Android, and it seems like it allows the user to pick photos that the URI are `content://xxxx` As you can see here, it's only happening since some days ago (when I published SDK 49 upgrade). Is there a workaround for this? Maybe some available flag to switch back to the old UI version, where files with `content://` uris were not visible. Current code: ```js const options = { mediaTypes: ImagePicker.MediaTypeOptions.Images, allowsEditing: false, exif: true, quality: 0.91, }; ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync(options) ``` ### Environment ``` expo-env-info 1.0.5 environment info: System: OS: macOS 12.6.3 Shell: 5.8.1 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 16.19.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.19.0/bin/node Yarn: 1.22.19 - ~/.yarn/bin/yarn npm: 8.19.3 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.19.0/bin/npm Managers: CocoaPods: 1.11.3 - /usr/local/bin/pod SDKs: iOS SDK: Platforms: DriverKit 22.2, iOS 16.2, macOS 13.1, tvOS 16.1, watchOS 9.1 IDEs: Android Studio: 2022.3 AI-223.8836.35.2231.10406996 Xcode: 14.2/14C18 - /usr/bin/xcodebuild npmPackages: expo: ^49.0.7 => 49.0.7 react: 18.2.0 => 18.2.0 react-native: 0.72.3 => 0.72.3 npmGlobalPackages: eas-cli: 4.1.2 expo-cli: 6.3.10 Expo Workflow: managed ``` "expo-image-picker": "~14.3.2",

@participant1 In my case, that's not the error I'm getting.

As far as I know, Android is now allowing the user to pick photos that are not local files, but files in "other sites" (like in Whatsapp), and that's why it's failing.

I just asked ChtGPT:


In Android, both `content://` and `file://` are URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) schemes used to reference resources, but they are typically used for different purposes:

1. **content://**:
The `content://` scheme is used to access data provided by Content Providers in Android. Content Providers are a way for different apps to share data with each other. They encapsulate the data and provide a standardized way to interact with it. Content Providers can be used to share data like contacts, media files, and other structured data between apps. When you use a `content://` URI, you are essentially requesting data from a Content Provider.

Example:
```
content://com.example.provider/contacts
```

2. **file://**:
The `file://` scheme is used to reference local files on the device's storage. This scheme is used when you want to work with files directly on the device's file system. However, starting from Android 7.0 (Nougat) and above, there are restrictions on using file URIs to access files outside your app's private directory. This is due to security concerns, as accessing arbitrary files could potentially lead to data leaks and unauthorized access.

Example:
```
file:///storage/emulated/0/Documents/example.txt
```

100% old school.

1. I make a change in the app
2. I create a new version (package json, and app.json)
3. I build `eas build -p android --local`
4. I submit it `eas submit -p android`
5. I push it from `internal testing` to `production` in Google Play Console Developers

Period.

Then, some times, only few times when it's really necessary, I go to change a value I have in a database which is the "last app version recommeded".

Every time the app is open in a device, it check this value in the database. If the user is opening an app version `18.0.0`, and the recommededn in the database is `19.0.0`, I show to the user a text saying: "This app is too old, update it, click here" (which opens the App Store so they can click in "Update")
